## Comparability note

Four of the five carriers (Delta, United, Southwest, American) report on a calendar fiscal year ending Dec 31, 2024, so their FY2024 results are directly comparable [DOC-1]. **Alaska Air Group is not fully comparable on a like-for-like basis**: it closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and consolidated Hawaiian only from that date, contributing $869 million of revenue and a $113 million net loss to Alaska's FY2024 results [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 therefore blends ~8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of the combined entity; excluding Hawaiian, Alaska's implied revenue would be ~$10,866M and net income ~$508M. This affects Alaska's scale and margin comparisons but does not change the ranking conclusion.

## Absolute profitability (FY2024, $ in millions)

| Airline | Operating income | Net income |
|---|---|---|
| Delta | $5,995 | $3,457 [DOC-1] |
| United | $5,096 | $3,149 [DOC-1] |
| American | $2,614 | $846 [DOC-1] |
| Alaska | $570 | $395 [DOC-1] |
| Southwest | $321 | $465 [DOC-1] |

Delta leads on both operating income ($5,995M vs. United's $5,096M) and net income ($3,457M vs. United's $3,149M) [DOC-1].

## Margin profitability

- **Delta:** operating margin 9.7% ($5,995 / $61,643), net margin 5.6% [DOC-1]
- **United:** operating margin 8.9% ($5,096 / $57,063), net margin 5.5% [DOC-1]
- **Alaska:** operating margin 4.9% ($570 / $11,735), net margin 3.4% [DOC-1] — roughly 4.7% net margin excluding the Hawaiian drag [DOC-2]
- **American:** operating margin 4.8% ($2,614 / $54,211), net margin 1.6% [DOC-1]
- **Southwest:** operating margin 1.2% ($321 / $27,483), net margin 1.7%; note Southwest's net income ($465M) exceeded its operating income ($321M), indicating non-operating gains rather than core earnings [DOC-1]

## Conclusion

Delta is the most profitable of the five on every measure — largest absolute operating income, largest absolute net income, and highest operating and net margins — with United a close second and Southwest and American the weakest. The Alaska/Hawaiian partial-period consolidation is the only comparability caveat, and it does not alter the ranking.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — highest FY2024 net income ($3,457M vs. United $3,149M), highest operating income ($5,995M), and highest operating margin (~9.7%) and net margin (~5.6%) of the five carriers (note: Alaska's FY2024 includes Hawaiian only from Sept 18, 2024, so it is not fully comparable).
